title: Longest Balanced Substring II
summary: Given a string s made up of 'a', 'b', and 'c', find the length of the longest substring where each distinct character appears an equal number of times.
statement: Given a string s made up of 'a', 'b', and 'c', find the length of the longest substring where each distinct character appears an equal number of times.
constraints: s contains up to 100,000 characters, each a, b, or c.
A substring is balanced when all characters present in it have equal frequency.
Return the maximum balanced substring length.
hints: A balanced substring contains exactly one, two, or all three possible characters.
Handle runs for one character, prefix differences inside two-character segments, and a pair of global prefix differences for all three.
Equal prefix-difference states mark a substring with equal relevant counts; excluded third characters split the two-character cases.
The three cases exhaust every possible distinct-character set and each prefix identity is equivalent to equal frequencies.
editorial: The three cases exhaust every possible distinct-character set and each prefix identity is equivalent to equal frequencies.

tests.explanation: The substring abba has two copies each of a and b, so its length is four.
The substring abc has one copy of each character, giving length three.
